module: Module 1 — Input/output, variables and basic arithmetic
title: Read from STDIN, Write to STDOUT
statement: Practice reading values from standard input and printing the required result. This starter uses two integers and prints their sum; follow the exact input/output contract of the assigned judge version.
note: The PDF gives only the platform problem title, not its full statement. Confirm the exact expected operation on HackerEarth before submission.

module: Module 1 — Input/output, variables and basic arithmetic
title: Solve Me First
statement: Given two integers, read them and print their sum.

module: Module 1 — Input/output, variables and basic arithmetic
title: 2235 — Add Two Integers
statement: Given two integers num1 and num2, return their sum. This is the standalone C version using standard input/output.
note: LeetCode's native submission expects the function int sum(int num1, int num2). This page provides a runnable standalone version.

module: Module 1 — Input/output, variables and basic arithmetic
title: 2651 — Calculate Delayed Arrival Time
statement: Given arrivalTime and delayedTime in hours on a 24-hour clock, print the delayed arrival time.
note: LeetCode function signature: int findDelayedArrivalTime(int arrivalTime, int delayedTime).

module: Module 1 — Input/output, variables and basic arithmetic
title: 2739 — Total Distance Traveled
statement: Given mainTank and additionalTank, print the total distance traveled. A truck travels 10 km per litre; every 5 litres consumed from the main tank allow 1 litre from the additional tank, if available.
note: LeetCode function signature: int distanceTraveled(int mainTank, int additionalTank).

title: Conditional Statements in C
statement: Read an integer and print its English word for values 1 through 9; otherwise print Greater than 9.

title: 2413 — Smallest Even Multiple
statement: Print the smallest positive number that is divisible by n and is even.
note: LeetCode function signature: int smallestEvenMultiple(int n).

title: Grading Students
statement: For each grade, round up to the next multiple of 5 only if the grade is at least 38 and the difference is less than 3.

title: Roy and Profile Picture
statement: For each photo, print ACCEPTED if its width and height are both at least the required length L; otherwise print UPLOAD ANOTHER. If both dimensions are larger than L but unequal, print CROP IT.

title: FizzBuzz
statement: Print numbers from 1 to n. For multiples of 3 print Fizz, multiples of 5 print Buzz, and multiples of both print FizzBuzz.
note: Check divisibility by 15 first; otherwise 3 or 5 would capture those values.

title: For Loop in C
statement: Read two integers a and b. For each integer in the inclusive range, print its English word for 1–9, otherwise print EVEN or ODD.

title: 1342 — Number of Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero
statement: Count operations to reduce num to zero: divide by 2 when even; subtract 1 when odd.
note: LeetCode function signature: int numberOfSteps(int num).

title: 2169 — Count Operations to Obtain Zero
statement: Repeatedly subtract the smaller of two positive numbers from the larger until one becomes zero. Print the number of operations.
note: LeetCode function signature: int countOperations(int num1, int num2).

title: 1523 — Count Odd Numbers in an Interval Range
statement: Print the number of odd integers in the inclusive interval [low, high].
note: LeetCode function signature: int countOdds(int low, int high).

title: 2652 — Sum Multiples
statement: Print the sum of all positive integers from 1 through n that are divisible by 3, 5, or 7.
note: LeetCode function signature: int sumOfMultiples(int n).

title: Number Line Jumps
statement: Given starting positions x1, x2 and jump distances v1, v2, determine whether both kangaroos land at the same position after the same number of jumps.

module: Module 4 — Digit extraction and number manipulation
title: Digit Sum
statement: Read a non-negative integer and print the sum of its decimal digits.

module: Module 4 — Digit extraction and number manipulation
title: Find Digits
statement: For each test case, count how many digits of n divide n evenly. Ignore zero digits.

module: Module 4 — Digit extraction and number manipulation
title: 1281 — Subtract the Product and Sum of Digits
statement: Print the product of the digits of n minus the sum of its digits.
note: LeetCode function signature: int subtractProductAndSum(int n).

module: Module 4 — Digit extraction and number manipulation
title: 2520 — Count the Digits That Divide a Number
statement: Count the non-zero digits of num that divide num evenly.
note: LeetCode function signature: int countDigits(int num).

module: Module 4 — Digit extraction and number manipulation
title: 9 — Palindrome Number
statement: Print true if the integer reads the same forward and backward; otherwise print false.
note: LeetCode function signature: bool isPalindrome(int x).

module: Module 4 — Digit extraction and number manipulation
title: 7 — Reverse Integer
statement: Reverse the digits of a signed 32-bit integer. If the reversed value overflows the signed 32-bit range, print 0.
note: LeetCode function signature: int reverse(int x).

module: Module 5 — Factors, divisibility and mathematical loops
title: 231 — Power of Two
statement: Print true if n is a positive power of two; otherwise print false.
note: LeetCode function signature: bool isPowerOfTwo(int n).

module: Module 5 — Factors, divisibility and mathematical loops
title: 326 — Power of Three
statement: Print true if n is a positive power of three; otherwise print false.
note: LeetCode function signature: bool isPowerOfThree(int n).

module: Module 5 — Factors, divisibility and mathematical loops
title: Factorial!
statement: Read n and print n factorial. This implementation uses unsigned long long; keep n within the range where the result fits.
note: The largest n that fits in unsigned long long is 20.

module: Module 5 — Factors, divisibility and mathematical loops
title: Count Divisors
statement: Read a positive integer n and count its positive divisors.

module: Module 5 — Factors, divisibility and mathematical loops
title: Prime Numbers
statement: Read n and print all prime numbers from 2 through n, one per line.
note: If your HackerEarth test case asks for a different format (such as checking one number), adapt the output to that statement.

module: Module 5 — Factors, divisibility and mathematical loops
title: 507 — Perfect Number
statement: A positive integer is perfect when the sum of its positive divisors excluding itself equals the number. Print true or false.
note: LeetCode function signature: bool checkPerfectNumber(int num).

module: Module 6 — Nested loops: online judge problems
title: Staircase
statement: Print a right-aligned staircase of height n using # characters.

module: Module 6 — Nested loops: online judge problems
title: Printing Pattern Using Loops
statement: Print the HackerRank concentric square number pattern for a given n. The outermost ring contains n and the center contains 1.

title: 1. Print a Solid Square
statement: Print n rows and n columns of asterisks.
note: Outer loop controls rows; inner loop prints n stars per row.

title: 2. Print a Right-Angled Triangle
statement: Row i contains exactly i asterisks.

title: 3. Print an Inverted Triangle
statement: The first row has n stars; each following row has one fewer.

title: 4. Print a Number Triangle
statement: On row i, print integers from 1 through i separated by spaces.

title: 5. Print a Repeated-Number Triangle
statement: On row i, print the number i exactly i times.

title: 6. Print a Consecutive-Number Triangle
statement: Print consecutive positive integers across rows of lengths 1, 2, 3, and so on.

title: 7. Print a Right-Aligned Star Triangle
statement: Row i has n-i leading spaces followed by i asterisks.

title: 8. Print a Centered Pyramid
statement: Row i has n-i spaces and 2i-1 asterisks.

title: 9. Print an Inverted Centered Pyramid
statement: Row i has i-1 spaces and 2(n-i)+1 asterisks.

title: 10. Print a Hollow Square
statement: Print stars on the boundary of an n-by-n square and spaces inside.
note: Boundary condition: first/last row OR first/last column.

title: 11. Print a Hollow Right-Angled Triangle
statement: Print stars in the first column, on the diagonal, and across the final row.

title: 12. Print a Multiplication Table Grid
statement: At row i and column j, print i multiplied by j.

title: 13. Print a Checkerboard
statement: Print an n-by-n checkerboard. Top-left is X and adjacent cells alternate.

title: 14. Print Floyd's Triangle
statement: Fill triangular rows with consecutive positive integers starting at 1.
note: This intentionally has the same output pattern as Question 6; it is retained as a separate assignment item.

title: 15. Print a Butterfly Pattern
statement: Given odd n, print a butterfly with widening upper wings and a mirrored lower half.
note: For each row, print the same number of stars on both sides. The center gap shrinks as the wings widen, then the pattern mirrors.

title: 16. Print a Diamond Pattern
statement: Print a centered diamond with n rows in the upper half, including the widest row, then n-1 shrinking rows.
